result.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
result.comment: 30 pages, 7 figures. Code available as ancillary files
result.summary: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions. We ask when such a quantity is identifiable from an experiment's access, continuous in the mechanism and certifiable from finite data, and answer exactly for a deliberately demanding case - the integrated information $\varphi$ of integrated information theory - in stochastic networks of four and five units with known ground truth. Behavior can be silent: a recurrent and a feed-forward network with identical input-output laws at their response delay carry 0.28 and 0 bits, yet internal recordings separate them within 4-53 trials. Partial access can be just as blind: in our examples, units left out of a one-step recording impose precision floors of 0.30-1.02 bits that no sample size lowers, and in all-but-self parity networks, recordings of any length see several hidden units only through the product of their fidelities - a symmetry that one intervention broke in exact checks. The measure has sharp edges: because $\varphi$ selects a partition, and the cause and effect it specifies, by one criterion and reports another, infinitesimal changes of mechanism that cross an edge change it by 25-100% at 99% of the edges we found in random networks, and about 1% of surrogate models that fit interventional data almost perfectly misreport it by more than 20%. One-sided claims survive: the same data certify a lower bound on both sides of an edge, and we prove $\varphi>1.004$ bits throughout a 64-dimensional region of mechanisms and certify it from about $10^7$ controlled transitions with false-certificate probability at most $α$. Measurability is thus a design question with computable answers.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究在有限、部分且含噪的干预下，整合信息 φ 这类机制层面量何时可识别、对机制连续并可被有限数据认证，并在四、五个单元的随机网络中给出行为等价、部分观测盲区、机制边界突变及单侧下界认证的示例与证明。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「机制量能否从有限干预与部分内部记录中被识别和认证」的框架，可能启发 LVR 中对 latent 内容是否被因果使用、以及内部状态贡献在部分可观测下能否可靠评估的讨论；但 φ 与视觉推理相距较远，可迁移性需核查。
